This is more of a neutral review, in terms of would i recommend this game. They are a lot of factors that will affect whether this game is worth your time, to me those factors and slightly in favour of, "Yes I would give this game a try". 

Price: 

The price is pretty ludicrous, especially so long after release, the DLC price also reflects this ambitious decision to charge an unreasonable amount of money for content which is repeatable at best. I could argue that the Sandbox alone makes this game at least in the £25 range; but ultimately the content is barren and its really one of the big things holding this game back from great success. 3/10

Story: 

The story is nothing revolutionary and you likely will forget all about it once you get to the current end-game; which at this point in time is the Expeditions, and furthermore, The Trial of Traya Gratar. Both of which are repeatable and dont add a whole lot to the current landscape of the story; although the Trials do add some more lore to an interesting faction non-the less. However, looter shooters are notorious for their wonky story-telling and with that said i dont think this is even a factor of why you shouldn't purchase or not. 3/10

End-game content: Repeatable, Not as rewarding as it should be, grindy to the point of not wanting to play anymore, and being extremely bored. If the end-game content was diverse enough, it would be a hit for me as that's mostly the only thing holding me back from continuous play. As it stands right now though, its just not up to the standards of other Looter Shooters, in terms of the diversity and reward in the end-game. 6/10

Sandbox & Build-crafting: 

This is where the game shines, the sandbox, from enemy types and attacks, to how you tackle those attacks and advances is extremely well done, better than any looter shooter that's out there by far. The build-crafting is reminiscent of The Division 2 - but simplified down a touch, and way more rewarding. The array of abilities and extensive complexity to play each class in different ways is something no other looter shooters really accomplishes. The power fantasy is definitely met in this game, and you feel as strong as you should be, with so many options how to play across 4 unique classes, there's honestly no downside about this section from me. 15/10

Loot System: 

As of right now the game is too grindy (yes i'm serious). This allows the game to not only widdle out casual players, but also a lot of hardcore players due to frustration. Nerfing drop-rates across the board in the only really viable end-game activity isn't a smart move, when the game still isn't in a state of stability in terms of daily players. Apocalypse gear was a nice step in the right direction to incentive a re-grind of current gear, however, when that gear is only obtainable after 100s of hours of game-play - combined with repeating the same activity over and over, its a vicious loop that gradually makes you loose interest in what you were chasing for in the first place.  Allowing players to focus loot to an extent might have relieved this - as of right now there is no word on any matters which is a shame. 

Developers and Communication: 

An often over-looked topic, but one that is important is the communication to the players. In this case the developers haven't been posting updates in seemingly weeks and weeks, and frankly its no surprise given how they choose to convey ideas in there posts. In the dev post that brought the nerf to the Traya Gratar final boss - they described it as 'Something they cannot change due to engine limitations', and that, 'we see the farming of the final boss as manipulation and exploitation'. While no-one received or receives bans, or anything like that for this, again choosing to label your community as Exploiters, doesn't send a good message for a game that got brought back from the Grave especially. 

TLDR; If you want a game with an amazing sandbox, build-crafting and fun new ways to fight, this is it. It is purely a game-play experience and one you reply to enjoy said game-play. Regardless to that, there are a lot of downsides and a few simple changes could alleviate that and allow for some replay-ability in this game. Changes for loot focusing, further adaptations to end-game content, and more communication from the Developers might allow for some much needed help. 

It's sad because this game is very good, but also very frustrating at the same time, its a real gem, and all it needs is some very minor changes to allow for more replay-ability and overall player enjoyment.

10/10. Outriders is honestly one of the most underrated games on Steam.

The combat is incredibly satisfying, every class feels powerful, and the ability combinations make every fight exciting. The loot system keeps you coming back for "just one more mission," and creating different builds is addictive. Unlike a lot of modern looter shooters, this game respects your time and focuses on being fun.

The campaign surprised me with how engaging it was, the world is interesting, and the endgame offers plenty of challenges if you enjoy chasing the perfect build. Playing with friends makes it even better, but it's also a fantastic solo experience.

It's a shame this game never got the recognition it deserved. If you're even slightly interested in looter shooters or action RPGs, you're doing yourself a disservice by skipping Outriders.

**10/10 – One of the best looter shooters ever made. Highly recommended.**
